hypotheses.claim: Effect safety requires typed release-time admission over authority, closure, epochs, selection, revocation and recovery rather than a destructive-syntax ban alone.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A sufficiently restrictive non-destructive model IR plus static capabilities is enough.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real sandbox/OS tests show omitted release-time dimensions add no failures after controlling capability scope.

hypotheses.claim: EffectIntent and EffectPermit should be different types; permits must be opaque host-minted handles bound to exact intent/scope/epoch.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A signed or validated model-serializable authorization object is equally safe and simpler.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial confused-deputy/replay/substitution tests show no measurable security benefit from opacity/non-constructibility.

hypotheses.claim: Required context is an operation-scoped causal-closure obligation, not a global permanent prompt pin.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Global mandatory pins are simpler and have negligible cognitive/resource cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target Qwen traces show global pins cause no measurable context, latency, attention or task-quality penalty over operation-scoped inclusion.

hypotheses.claim: Required-context inclusion should guarantee candidate availability but must not guarantee GWT victory or model-internal uptake.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Critical evidence should bypass competition and be forced into the workspace.
hypotheses.falsifier: Forced critical-evidence workspace inclusion outperforms competitive inclusion without increasing stale/context-invalid errors under matched budgets.

hypotheses.claim: CASAR route choice and MCAAT admissibility must be separate: a memory can be retrievable yet inadmissible for a consequential path.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Retrieval confidence/provenance can directly determine admissibility.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real workloads show a single retrieval score matches typed admissibility decisions across exact, approximate, salience and external-evidence roles.

hypotheses.claim: Utility credit needs ITEM/PATH/ASSEMBLY/UNKNOWN scope; UNKNOWN credit must not reinforce all surfaced memories.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One downstream reward can safely train a shared salience field with enough decay/regularization.
hypotheses.falsifier: Oracle-free target tests show scalar reward matches scoped credit on rare-case retention, false attractors and poisoned-memory resistance.

hypotheses.claim: Record authenticity and selection integrity are independent; both must be receipted before consequential use.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Authenticated records are sufficient because selector manipulation is detectable downstream.
hypotheses.falsifier: Live ClayGraph/UnifiedDB selection attacks cannot change consequential candidate sets while all records remain authentic.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent memory defense must include use-time/context-sensitive admission because write-time filtering misses compositional and dormant-trigger harms.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Strong enough write-time sanitation makes use-time admission redundant.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent reproduction shows modern write-time defenses close L2/L3 composition/trigger attacks without use-time context checks.

hypotheses.claim: FRANK physical architecture should optimize a PlacementVector after semantic/authority constraints rather than choose one database/process topology globally.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A single colocated runtime/database is globally simpler and faster without meaningful fault/security loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real FRANK traces show one fixed placement Pareto-dominates adaptive placements across latency, recovery, memory, energy and fault radius.

hypotheses.claim: A WASI-style no-ambient-authority sandbox is a strong candidate lowering for generated foreign code under Clay effect closure.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Conventional process isolation plus filesystem permissions is sufficient and less complex.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched escape/utility tests show no containment advantage from capability imports or unacceptable utility/performance loss.

hypotheses.claim: Constructive-only Clay primitives can reduce reachable damage only if foreign-code/tool descendants obey EffectiveEffects(child) subseteq Effects(parent).
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Host validation at the top-level effect call alone is sufficient.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial child-language tests find no authority amplification even without compositional effect closure.

hypotheses.claim: System WorkspaceEpisode, internal Qwen workspace uptake and effect authority are three separable causal stages.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A model-internal privileged representation fully mediates system workspace effects and can be treated as the same stage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target Qwen interventions cannot dissociate system selection, internal uptake and effect release under fixed projections/capabilities.

hypotheses.claim: Android should be a semantic/resource conformance target, not a source of general FRANK performance claims without matched Linux replication.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: ARM Android measurements generalize adequately to the Linux reference runtime for architectural tuning.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated matched experiments show stable ordering/effect sizes across Linux and Android for the proposed optimizations.

hypotheses.claim: The next Android experiment should gate scarce device runs behind CI proof that the quantized Qwen-class package builds and loads.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Direct device iteration yields more information despite quota cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: CI preflight fails to predict device integration failures and adds more delay than saved device invocations.

hypotheses.claim: Full-model Clay adaptation must train authority/admissibility distinctions, not merely compact syntax, or the runtime will carry nearly all safety burden.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Language semantics can remain external; model training only needs efficient Clay token production.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched target-model experiments show no benefit in semantic execution, destructive-proposal rate or authority-negative behavior from typed-admission training.

hypotheses.claim: No FRANK emergence claim should use recurrence/persistence until salience-attractor and selection-confound controls are negative.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Stable recurrent multi-scale patterns remain emergence evidence even when adaptive salience contributes strongly.
hypotheses.falsifier: Prospective E-CERT2 analysis identifies macro causal contribution that survives frozen/shuffled/anti-attractor controls and mechanistic rescue.
